name: get-flags
description: Without flagKey: search and browse feature flags; returns a paginated summary per flag (key, name, description, kind, tags, temporary, archived, deprecated, maintainer, and whether targeting is on) in one environment. Always set env to the environment the user named. With flagKey: get one flag scoped to env, with the full targeting tree (rules, individual targets, fallthrough, prerequisites) and variations. Each rule and each clause carries an `_id`; pass them as ruleId and clauseId to update-targeting-rules (addValuesToClause, removeValuesFromClause, updateClause) or create-approval-request to edit a clause in place.

env.description: Environment key. Always set to the environment the user named.

flagKey.description: The feature flag key. Omit to list flags; pass to get one flag.

projectKey.description: The project key

name: create-flag
description: Create a new feature flag in a project. Defaults to a boolean temporary flag. After creation the flag is off in all environments. Multivariate flags require defaults. If the response has needsTeamMaintainer, the flag was not created: ask the user which of the returned teams should own it, then retry with maintainerTeamKey. Set defaults.offVariation to the index of the value your code falls back to, so the new flag behaves like the code while off and needs no approval to stay that way. defaults.onVariation is the index served when targeting is on. To change them later, call update-off-variation (envs ["*"], fallthroughVariationIndex) and update-flag with updateDefaultVariation for new environments.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

name: update-flag
description: Update a flag's top-level settings and variations without changing environment targeting. It takes no environment: names, descriptions, tags, maintainers, and variations are project-wide, so never ask for one. Accepted instruction kinds: updateName, updateDescription, addTags and removeTags (values array), makeFlagTemporary, makeFlagPermanent, updateMaintainerMember, updateMaintainerTeam, addCustomProperties, replaceCustomProperties, removeCustomProperties, updateDefaultVariation, addVariation, updateVariation. updateDefaultVariation takes OnVariationValue and/or OffVariationValue (PascalCase), the variation values themselves, not indexes; for example {"kind":"updateDefaultVariation","OnVariationValue":true,"OffVariationValue":false}. Repeating an addVariation with the same value, name and description is a no-op; the same value with a different name or description is rejected (use updateVariation). Turning a flag on or off is environment-scoped: use toggle-flag, not turnFlagOn or turnFlagOff here. Pass either instructions or variationJsonSchema, never both; make two separate calls.

dryRun.description: If true, the patch will be validated but not persisted. Returns a preview of the flag after the patch is applied.

flagKey.description: The feature flag key. The key identifies the flag in your code.

projectKey.description: The project key

variationJsonSchema.description: JSON schema that replaces the flag's variation schema.

name: recommend-flag
description: Record an ADVISORY recommendation on whether a code change should be placed behind a LaunchDarkly feature flag. This tool is READ-ONLY: it does not create, modify, toggle, or delete any flag. Call it exactly once, as the final step, after you have understood the change and explored the surrounding code. The recommendation is what CI parses to post a pull-request check.

recommend.description: true if the change should be released behind a feature flag, false if it should not

verdict.description: The finer-grained outcome. suggested = a new flag is warranted (pairs with recommend: true). reuse-existing = the change should be gated behind an EXISTING flag that already covers this same unreleased feature rather than a new one — set reuse_flag_key (pairs with recommend: true). already-flagged = the change is already protected by a flag in the diff or an off/mid-rollout ancestor gate (recommend: false). not-suited = there is genuinely nothing to flag: pure refactor, docs, tests, dependency bump, or build/CI/tooling change (recommend: false).

reuse_flag_key.description: Set ONLY when verdict is reuse-existing: the key of the existing flag to gate this change behind (the flag that already covers this feature). Omit for every other verdict.

confidence.description: Confidence in the recommendation, calibrated to how clear the signal is and how much surrounding code you verified

risk.description: Optional. Blast radius / severity of the change itself, independent of confidence. low = small additive isolated change; medium = modified business logic / moderate blast radius; high = cross-cutting, API-contract, data-migration, or auth/payments/data-integrity change.

reasons.description: Concise, evidence-based justifications. Each should cite the specific file, symbol, or behavior that drove the verdict.

name: create-automated-rollout-config
description: Record an automated rollout config for a feature-flagged change. Use it only for AutomatedRollout requests. The guarding flag must already exist. repoFullName, prNumber, and prUrl are optional: pass the PR the user names or one you just filed, and omit them when there is none. Each environment either pins an override rollout or follows its release policy after the merge. releaseType is only override or policy; immediate, progressive, and guarded are override.releaseMethod values. An immediate release passes only environmentKey, with no releaseType or override. Stages have exactly allocation and durationMillis; allocation is thousandths of a percent, so 10% over one hour is {"allocation":10000,"durationMillis":3600000}. The context kind field is override.rolloutContextKindKey. For policy environments the response can include warnings about a missing or incomplete policy: surface them in generated comments, do not describe the release as a clean policy rollout, and do not add tags to make a policy match. Returns created, config_id, flag_key, the normalized environments, and warnings.

endingVariationId.description: Variation a multi-variate flag rolls out to. Boolean flags default to true.

metricGroupKeys.description: Metric groups that gate a guarded rollout.

metricKeys.description: Metrics that gate a guarded rollout. Guarded needs metricKeys or metricGroupKeys.

releaseMethod.description: immediate turns the flag on and takes no stages or metrics; progressive ramps through stages; guarded ramps through stages gated on metrics.

rollbackOnRegression.description: Roll back automatically when a guarded metric regresses.

rolloutContextKindKey.description: Context kind the rollout allocates by.

allocation.description: Thousandths of a percent: 100000 is 100%, 10000 is 10%, 1000 is 1%.

durationMillis.description: Monitoring window in milliseconds. Must be greater than 0 for every stage, including the last.

stages.description: Required for progressive and guarded. Allocations must be positive and strictly increasing. Guarded caps every stage at 50000 and promotes to 100% after the last stage, so do not add a 100000 stage; progressive usually ends at 100000. Each stage has exactly allocation and durationMillis, e.g. {"allocation":10000,"durationMillis":3600000} for 10% over one hour.

override.description: Inline rollout for releaseType override. For an immediate release, omit override and releaseType and pass only environmentKey.

releaseType.description: Only override or policy. override (default) pins the rollout in override; policy waits for the PR merge and the flag's first evaluation, then applies the environment's release policy. Do not pass override with policy. immediate, progressive, and guarded are override.releaseMethod values.

flagKey.description: Key of the guarding flag, which must already exist.

projectKey.description: LaunchDarkly project key.

startingVariationId.description: Variation a multi-variate flag rolls out from. Boolean flags default to false; multi-variate flags need both variation IDs, and setting only one is rejected.

With metricKey: get full details for one metric. To find which metric a metric version ID belongs to (experiments reference metrics by version), list with versionIds.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

sort.description: createdAt, name, connectionCount, or activeConnectionCount. Prefix with - for descending order.

versionIds.description: Metric version IDs. Returns the metrics these versions belong to; each result carries its versionId.

name: create-metric
description: Create a custom, pageview, click, or trace metric. To count each unit's distinct values of a warehouse column, set measureType distinct and name the column in unitAggregationField; valueColumn is only for measureType value.

dataSourceKey.description: Warehouse data source of the denominator term. Omit to use the metric's dataSourceKey.

eventName.description: Event key of the denominator term.

filters.description: Count only events matching context attribute or event property clauses. Custom metrics only. A group joins clauses or further groups with and/or.

measureType.description: distinct counts each unit's unique values of the unitAggregationField column; it does not use valueColumn.

unitAggregationField.description: Required with measureType distinct: the warehouse column whose unique values are counted per unit, for example ORDER_ID.

windowEndOffset.description: End of the measurement window, in milliseconds after the unit's first exposure.

windowStartOffset.description: Start of the measurement window, in milliseconds after the unit's first exposure.

winsorIncludeImputed.description: Count the 0 imputed for units without events when computing the winsorization bounds.

winsorLowerPercentile.description: Clamp unit values below this percentile, in the open interval (0, 100).

winsorUpperPercentile.description: Clamp unit values above this percentile, in the open interval (0, 100).

denominator.description: Denominator term of a ratio metric; the metric's own event is the numerator term. Custom metrics on a warehouse data source only: requires dataSourceKey.

excludeUnitsWithoutEvents.description: Leave units that sent no event out of the analysis instead of counting them as 0.

filters.description: Count only events matching context attribute or event property clauses. Custom metrics only. A group joins clauses or further groups with and/or.

measureType.description: distinct counts each unit's unique values of the unitAggregationField column; it does not use valueColumn.

percentile.description: Analyze this percentile of unit values instead of the mean. Requires excludeUnitsWithoutEvents: true.

projectKey.description: Project key. If the user hasn't named one, ask; don't guess.

traceQuery.description: Trace query of a trace metric, for example service.name = "checkout".

traceValueLocation.description: Where a trace metric with measureType value reads its number, for example duration.

unitAggregationField.description: Required with measureType distinct: the warehouse column whose unique values are counted per unit, for example ORDER_ID.

valueColumn.description: Warehouse column holding the numeric value for measureType value.

windowEndOffset.description: End of the measurement window, in milliseconds after the unit's first exposure.

windowStartOffset.description: Start of the measurement window, in milliseconds after the unit's first exposure.

winsorIncludeImputed.description: Count the 0 imputed for units without events when computing the winsorization bounds.

winsorLowerPercentile.description: Clamp unit values below this percentile, in the open interval (0, 100).
